meeting_header: Date: 2026-11-29 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m\nAttendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Zhou (Redwood SE), Leah Kim (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (Redwood TPM); Daniel Hsu (Oakridge Head of Security), Priya Menon (Oakridge Platform Eng Manager), Carlos Rivera (Oakridge DevOps), Sara Nguyen (Oakridge Compliance)
summary: Introductory security posture and deployment requirements call for Oakridge evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Main concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning, RBAC scoping, audit logging and retention, KMS key control and bring-your-own-key, data residency and retention policy. Discussed fallbacks, model variant routing, and minimum SLA needs. Agreed next steps: send SOC2 artifacts, schedule KMS deep dive, share pilot SOW and pricing.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. I can see folks from Oakridge, want to do quick intros and then jump into security posture and deployment questions.
[00:12] Daniel Hsu: Hi, Daniel Hsu, Head of Security at Oakridge. We own risk and compliance. Main thing for us is we need to understand how Redwood handles keys, auditability, and what evidence you can provide.
[00:22] Priya Menon: Priya here, platform manager. We're evaluating whether we can start with Hosted and later move to Dedicated or Private, but need to confirm encryption and SSO integration.
[00:31] Maya Patel: Totally. High level we support Hosted API for quick integration, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput and isolation, and Private for VPC/on-prem. Today Ethan and Leah are with me for the deeper infra questions.
[00:41] Ethan Zhou: Hi all. Quick note: sometimes our docs call the private option "Private Deployment" and folks see different names, so forgive the terms.
[00:50] Carlos Rivera: One thing: our security team mandates BYOK for any consumer-facing PII processing. Can Redwood support BYOK with our cloud KMS? We run Google KMS & Hashi Vault for some workloads.
[01:02] Leah Kim: Yes, we support customer-managed keys in Hosted via KMS integration. There's a couple of modes — you can bring keys or use Redwood-managed keys with HSM-backed encryption. For Dedicated and Private we give you control over the key lifecycle and rotation cadence.
[01:18] Sara Nguyen: Are the keys ever cached in plaintext on the inference nodes? That's a big red flag for our auditors.
[01:25] Ethan Zhou: No, keys are not persisted in plain text. We use envelope encryption: data keys are generated and encrypted with the KMS CMK. The runtime only holds the wrapped data key in memory and uses accelerated crypto primitives. That said, I'll follow up with the architecture diagram to show the exact handoff.
[01:38] Daniel Hsu: Can you share SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence? We need to attach them to our vendor risk assessment.
[01:47] Maya Patel: Absolutely. We'll share the SOC2 report and the ISO attestation. Note: redactions in SOC2 are typical, but we'll provide the artifact and a security packet.
[01:55] Priya Menon: On SSO, we run Okta and need SAML2.0 + SCIM for provisioning. How mature is your SSO support and can you enforce org-scoped RBAC?
[02:07] Ethan Zhou: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is customizable — you can create roles that map to scopes, and restrict token-level permissions per route. There's a subtlety: in Hosted, some lower-level infra controls are multi-tenant, so we expose RBAC at the control plane and tenant level. Dedicated/Private gives you full control over cluster-level RBAC.
[02:30] Carlos Rivera: Ok, so for Hosted we'd still be able to restrict what our engineers can do via the Console?
[02:35] Leah Kim: Yes, you can set console roles, API key scopes, and route-level permissions. For stricter isolation we recommend Dedicated where you get reserved capacity and isolated compute.
[02:46] Daniel Hsu: Audit logs — what's the retention and do they include token-level request metadata (caller, model, prompt hash, timing)? Auditors want immutable logs for 12 months.
[02:58] Ethan Zhou: Hosted has configurable retention — default 90 days, can extend with add-on retention up to one year or more. Logs capture request metadata, latency, model id, and anonymized prompt hashes. For Dedicated and Private we can route logs to your SIEM via syslog/Kinesis/GCS bucket; retention is then under your control.
[03:18] Sara Nguyen: You said anonymized prompt hashes. For some regulated flows we need the actual prompt for debugging. Is that possible?
[03:26] Maya Patel: We can provide configurable capture but there are data residency and privacy tradeoffs. For PII content, we'd recommend tokenization at the edge or local preprocessing. We'll outline options in the follow-up.
[03:36] Priya Menon: Network connectivity — can we VPC peering to Hosted or does that only exist for Private deployments? Latency matters for inference.
[03:44] Ethan Zhou: VPC peering for Hosted is limited by cloud provider. For low-latency, Dedicated in your region or Private VPC peering is recommended. Hosted can be accessed over private endpoints in some cloud regions; we'll need to validate your VPC setup.
[03:59] Priya Menon: Good. And does Redwood do model variant fallback? For reliability we want an automatic fallback to a smaller model if capacity's constrained.
[04:08] Leah Kim: Yes, routing policies can define fallback variants by latency/cost tiers. We can also run canary rollouts and automatic fallback rules.
[04:18] Daniel Hsu: Encryption at rest — confirm that all data at rest is encrypted and that log storage is encrypted and, if possible, customer-managed keys?
[04:27] Ethan Zhou: All data at rest is encrypted. For Hosted, logs and backups are encrypted with either Redwood-managed or customer-managed keys depending on plan. Dedicated and Private let you bring the CMK and manage rotation policies.
[04:37] Carlos Rivera: For KMS, what's the rotation/rotation policy? We do 90-day rotation for some keys.
[04:44] Leah Kim: Rotation can be automated via your KMS — Redwood supports scheduled rotation or manual rotations triggered by your ops. We'll document the recommended cadence and implications for active sessions and key caching.
[04:58] Daniel Hsu: How about auditability of key usage? We need to see who performed decrypt ops and when.
[05:05] Ethan Zhou: If you use your KMS, all decrypt/encrypt API calls are logged in your KMS audit. In addition, we log key-usage events at the request level and can stream them to your SIEM.
[05:18] Maya Patel: Quick pause — looks like we're at the high level. Daniel, what's your timeline and decision criteria? Is SOC2 enough or do you need additional attestations?
[05:27] Daniel Hsu: Timeline is Q1 POC. Decision criteria: must have SOC2 Type II, SSO + SCIM, BYOK for keys, RBAC mapping to our IAM, and network isolation options. If those check boxes are green, we run a pilot.
[05:40] Priya Menon: Also cost vs latency tradeoff — we need numbers on Dedicated throughput pricing.
[05:46] Tom Alvarez: We'll prepare a pilot SOW with expected throughput and pricing.
[05:51] Carlos Rivera: One more technical: How do you handle KV cache and in-memory context — any risk of cross-tenant leakage?
[05:59] Ethan Zhou: Isolation for KV cache is enforced per tenant; we do strict memory partitioning and zero-fill on deallocation. That said, we can provide an architecture note showing the memory safety checks and the test evidence.
[06:12] Sara Nguyen: Data retention policy — can we set different retention per dataset and ensure deletion on request? We need to meet right-to-be-forgotten requests within 30 days.
[06:22] Leah Kim: Yes, retention controls are configurable; for Hosted it's via the retention add-on and retention policies per route. For Dedicated/Private you have direct control. We'll also show the deletion workflow and audit trail.
[06:33] Daniel Hsu: Regarding logging integrity — do logs have tamper-evident features? WORM or signed logs?
[06:41] Ethan Zhou: We offer signed logs and append-only stores for customers that need WORM. For Hosted customers requiring tamper-evidence, we can enable signed log exports to your storage bucket.
[06:53] Maya Patel: Questions from Oakridge on compliance scoping — do you need us to fill out any questionnaires or is there a standard security review pack?
[07:01] Sara Nguyen: We'll need an SOC2 copy and answers to a security questionnaire; sometimes procurements ask for SIG or CAIQ.
[07:08] Maya Patel: We'll share our security packet and can do the SIG/CAIQ response.
[07:14] Daniel Hsu: Any third-party penetration testing results or bug-bounty program?
[07:19] Ethan Zhou: We run annual third-party pentests and have a vulnerability disclosure program; details will be in the security packet.
[07:27] Priya Menon: For Private deployments, how mature is the on-prem installer and upgrade cadence? We can't have frequent forced upgrades in production windows.
[07:36] Leah Kim: On-prem supports controlled upgrades; we coordinate windows and provide upgrade playbooks. For Private in air-gapped environments we provide offline bundles and step-by-step guidance.
[07:47] Carlos Rivera: Are there differences in observability? We need traces and token-level cost metrics.
[07:54] Tom Alvarez: The Console exposes token-level cost and latency breakdowns. For Dedicated/Private you can also ingest telemetry into your monitoring stack; we'll share the tracing hooks.
[08:05] Daniel Hsu: One final ask — can you expose per-route retention and per-route RBAC so that some routes (like PII) have stricter controls?
[08:15] Ethan Zhou: Yes, route-scoped configs are supported — retention, RBAC scopes, and model selection can be per-route. We'll include examples.
[08:25] Priya Menon: Great. On the legal side, do you support data residency controls for EU-only processing? We have EU customers.
[08:33] Leah Kim: We have region controls and can pin processing to regions (EU-only). For Hosted you choose the region and for Dedicated/Private you can deploy in specific regions.
[08:43] Daniel Hsu: Are there any blockers we should be aware of for SOC or procurement?
[08:47] Maya Patel: Not beyond the standard paperwork — SOC2, ISO, DPA and a security questionnaire. For BYOK and VPC peering we'll run a technical workstream in parallel.
[08:58] Sara Nguyen: Okay good. Let's recap next steps.
[09:02] Maya Patel: Recap — Redwood will share SOC2 and security packet; SEs to schedule KMS/network deep dive; Redwood to draft pilot SOW and pricing; Oakridge to share KMS provider and network diagram. Anything else?
[09:18] Daniel Hsu: Could you also include a short note about fallback models and how that impacts latency and cost?
[09:24] Tom Alvarez: Will do, we'll include expected latency numbers for fallback variants in the SOW.
[09:30] Maya Patel: Perfect. Thank you all, we'll send the materials and set the follow-up for early next week.
[09:36] Priya Menon: Thanks.
[09:38] Carlos Rivera: Thanks everyone.
[09:40] Ethan Zhou: Thanks, talk soon.
[09:43] [call ends]
